requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Configurator refused SPIKE_CLASH when both placed at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 on piece:0,0,0;half-n with drawer:0#0,0#cut. Rule: spike needs three bases meeting, drawer occupies cut face and blocks that junction. Built closest verified alternative: drawer on piece:0,0,0;half-n (key s) and spike:0#0,1|1,0|1,1 at next junction sharing the cell's edge, touching adjacency but not same corner. Mesh check clear.

finish.summary: Exact same-corner placement is blocked by configurator rule (SPIKE_CLASH). Built a 4-base cluster with drawer on half-n cell and spike at the adjacent three-base corner - the nearest touching arrangement the system allows, verified clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
